notes._about: Shipped default thresholds for j.tidy (E56_S06_T02). A project instance at project/configs/tidy-config.json REPLACES this file whole - there is no merging, the same way checklists.json and test-scope-map.json work. These numbers live in a config file rather than in skills/j-tidy/scripts/report.sh so that the script contains no threshold value at all: a missing config is reported as unavailable, never silently replaced by a built-in guess.
notes.retention_age_days: How old an entry's last commit must be before the report counts it as stale. 14 days is two sprints of inactivity: long enough that a worktree someone is still iterating on is not nagged about, short enough to catch the ones that were abandoned.
notes.worktree_count_ceiling: Crossing this makes the report say so prominently. 40 is an order of magnitude below the 229 measured in the Jenga repo on 2026-11-04 and roughly ten concurrent pieces of work with room to spare, so the nag starts long before the backlog becomes a disk problem.
notes.branch_count_ceiling: The branch count outruns the worktree count (350 vs 229 measured on 2026-11-04), because a branch survives its worktree. 80 is twice the worktree ceiling, which is the shape that gap actually takes.
notes.disk_ceiling_mb: 2048 MB (2 GB). A single worktree of the Jenga repo measured 31-85 MB, so 2 GB is on the order of 25-60 worktrees - the same scale as the count ceiling, reached from the direction that actually hurts the machine.
notes.report_max_rows_per_group: Rows listed per (verdict, population) group before the report truncates. Truncation ALWAYS prints how many entries were not shown; a silent cap reads as nothing there and is a reporting bug. 15 keeps a full sweep readable in one screen per group.
